name: Petra
strand: Cities of the Middle East & North Africa
scope: The Nabataean city carved into rose-red sandstone in a Jordanian gorge. T1: you reach Petra only by walking a narrow winding gorge over a kilometer long with walls up to 180 m high -- the crack in the cliffs is the SIQ. T2: at the Siq's end a 40 m temple-front glows out of the rock, nicknamed for treasure a legend says hides in its stone urn -- al-Khazneh, 'the Treasury' (Bedouin once shot at the urn hoping to spill the gold; the bullet marks and the treasure are LEGEND). T3 (invert the name): the 'Treasury' held no treasure -- it was a royal TOMB, most likely the mausoleum of King Aretas IV. T3: Petra's LARGEST carved monument is not the Treasury but a 50 m-wide facade up an 800-step climb -- Ad-Deir, the Monastery. T4: a desert city of ~30,000 survived with almost no rain because the Nabataeans cut channels, dams, and cisterns that captured flash-flood water -- a hidden ROCK-CUT WATER SYSTEM. T4: the rose-red color is the rock itself -- iron-bearing SANDSTONE banded red, pink, and orange. T4: Petra grew rich by taxing camel caravans hauling one precious cargo across Arabia -- INCENSE (frankincense and myrrh). T5: Petra faded after Rome opened SEA routes for incense and a 363 AD EARTHQUAKE wrecked its waterworks. T5: the West forgot Petra for ~600 years until 1812, when Swiss traveler Johann Ludwig Burckhardt talked his way in disguised as a pilgrim seeking Aaron's tomb. T5: high on a mountaintop above the city sits a carved open-air altar -- the High Place of Sacrifice.
source: Grokipedia (Petra) checked first; corroborated by en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petra, National Geographic 'Lost City of Petra', UNESCO WHS Petra listing. Verified: Siq >1 km / walls to 180 m; Khazneh 40 m, likely Aretas IV mausoleum, 1st c AD; Ad-Deir 50 m; ~30,000 pop with dam/cistern hydraulics; Burckhardt 22 Aug 1812.
framing_note: Place = Petra in every rung; the Treasury-is-really-a-tomb rung is the dinner-test twist and it INVERTS the misleading name. Accuracy rail: the urn-treasure and bullet-marks story is LEGEND, and the Treasury's exact function is inferred -- label both. Lead with the scene ('you walk a gorge...'), never 'What is Petra?'. Distractors stay live as OTHER real Petra features (the Monastery, the Royal Tombs, the Roman theatre) and other rock-cut sites (Lycian rock tombs, Ellora, Lalibela). No creature/food rungs -- the incense-trade rung stays a PLACE fact (Petra sat on the route), not a spice recipe.

name: Istanbul
strand: Cities of the Middle East & North Africa
scope: The only great city on two continents, split by the Bosphorus strait. T1: Istanbul is the only big city that sits on TWO continents at once, Europe and Asia, split by a narrow saltwater strait -- the BOSPHORUS. T2: for nearly 1,000 years the world's largest cathedral stood here, raised in just ~6 years in 537 AD by Emperor Justinian, its vast dome seeming to float -- HAGIA SOPHIA. T3: one building lived four lives -- Hagia Sophia went church, then MOSQUE (1453), then museum, then mosque again (2020). T3: beneath the streets hides a 'sunken palace' of water -- a Byzantine reservoir of 336 marble columns, two resting on carved MEDUSA HEADS -- the Basilica Cistern. T3: before Istanbul the city was CONSTANTINOPLE, and before that the Greek town of Byzantium. T4: the city held off attackers for a thousand years behind the triple THEODOSIAN WALLS -- until 1453, when Mehmed II's giant cannon finally breached them. T4: one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets is a roofed labyrinth of ~4,000 shops -- the GRAND BAZAAR. T4 (earth/geo): the Bosphorus is not a river but a STRAIT linking the Black Sea to the Mediterranean -- the only sea-gate out of the Black Sea. T5: Ottoman sultans ruled for ~400 years from TOPKAPI PALACE above the water. T5: the six-minaret SULTAN AHMED (Blue) Mosque faces Hagia Sophia across a square.
source: Grokipedia (Istanbul / Hagia Sophia) checked first; corroborated by Britannica 'Hagia Sophia', en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hagia_Sophia and /Basilica_Cistern. Verified: built 532-537 under Justinian, architects Anthemius & Isidorus, largest cathedral ~1,000 yrs, reconverted to mosque 2020; Basilica Cistern built post-Nika-Revolt 532 (336 columns / 2 Medusa bases widely documented).
framing_note: Place = Istanbul; the Medusa-head Basilica Cistern is the dinner-test payoff. Accuracy rail: Hagia Sophia = 537 AD, Justinian, largest cathedral for ~1,000 yrs -- keep those exact. Scene-led ('beneath the streets hides...'), never 'What is the capital of Turkey?'. Distractors live as other Istanbul sites (Galata Tower, Dolmabahce) and other straits (Dardanelles, Gibraltar, Hormuz). Turkish delight / kebabs are COOKING -- no food rung here.
history_overlap: The 1453 fall of Constantinople to Mehmed II may be a history-bank episode -- keep that rung anchored to the WALLS/cannon as a place fact; integrator should check for a duplicate siege ladder.

name: Cairo & the Giza Pyramids
strand: Cities of the Middle East & North Africa
scope: A ~20-million-person megacity whose western desert edge meets the last of the Seven Wonders. T1: on the desert rim of Cairo stand the last survivor of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world -- the three PYRAMIDS OF GIZA. T2 (invert the number): the Great Pyramid of Khufu rose 146 m and stayed the TALLEST building on Earth for ~3,800 years. T3: guarding the plateau is a limestone lion with a human face carved from a single rock ridge -- the GREAT SPHINX. T3: built from ~2.3 million blocks, the Great Pyramid is the ONLY one of the Seven Wonders still standing. T3: the pyramids sit on the Nile's WEST bank -- the side of the setting sun, where Egyptians placed their dead. T4: inside medieval 'Islamic Cairo' rise the Citadel of Saladin and AL-AZHAR, a university running since 972 AD. T4 (dinner-test): a living neighborhood spreads through Cairo's huge cemeteries, where families dwell among the tombs -- the CITY OF THE DEAD (al-Qarafa). T4: a medieval bazaar has traded here since the 14th century -- KHAN EL-KHALILI. T5 (earth/history): the pyramids' smooth white limestone CASING was stripped away to build medieval Cairo, exposing the stepped core we see now. T5: Cairo's Arabic name, al-Qahira, means 'the Victorious,' named for the planet Mars rising as the city was founded in 969. T5 (earth-process): the Nile's yearly flood laid black silt that made Egypt farmable -- Egyptians called their land KEMET, 'the Black Land.'
source: Grokipedia (Great Pyramid / Cairo) checked first; corroborated by en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Pyramid_of_Giza, Britannica 'Great Pyramid of Giza' and 'Pyramids of Giza'. Verified: original height 146.6 m, tallest structure ~3,800 yrs, only intact ancient Wonder, ~2.3 M blocks, Khufu's tomb; Sphinx ~73 m long / ~20 m high limestone; casing later removed.
framing_note: Place = Cairo/Giza; the City of the Dead (families living among the tombs) is the dinner-test. Accuracy rail: Great Pyramid = 146 m original, only surviving ancient Wonder, ~2.3 M blocks, Khufu -- keep exact; don't repeat the debunked 'slaves built it' line (skilled paid laborers). Distractors live as other pyramids (Djoser's Step Pyramid, the Bent Pyramid, Nubian/Meroe pyramids, Chichen Itza). Ful/koshari are COOKING -- no food rung.
history_overlap: The Al-Azhar founding (972) and the Kemet/Nile-flood civilization framing may touch a history-bank Egypt episode -- keep rungs anchored to the PLACE (plateau, west bank, Nile silt); integrator should check.

name: Jerusalem Old City
strand: Cities of the Middle East & North Africa
scope: A walled old city under one square kilometer, holy to three faiths. T1: Jerusalem's walled Old City -- barely 1 km2 -- is split into FOUR named quarters (Muslim, Christian, Jewish, Armenian). T2: a gold-domed octagonal shrine crowns the Temple Mount, the OLDEST surviving masterpiece of Islamic architecture -- the DOME OF THE ROCK. T3: the last standing remnant of the Second Temple, where Jews pray against ancient stones, is the WESTERN WALL. T3: the Christian Quarter centers on the church built over the traditional sites of Jesus's crucifixion and tomb -- the CHURCH OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE. T3 (dinner-test): a wooden ladder has sat unmoved on a ledge of the Holy Sepulchre since the 1700s because rival churches share the building and none may change a thing -- the IMMOVABLE LADDER. T4: the bare rock under the Dome is sacred to all three faiths -- Jews tie it to Abraham and the Temple; Muslims to Muhammad's Night-Journey ascent -- the FOUNDATION STONE. T4 (earth-material): by law, buildings must be faced in the local honey-colored limestone -- 'JERUSALEM STONE.' T4: an 8th-century-BC channel still runs beneath the city, cut through solid rock to bring the Gihon Spring inside the walls -- HEZEKIAH'S TUNNEL. T5: the traditional route Jesus walked to the cross, marked by Stations, is the VIA DOLOROSA.
source: Grokipedia (Old City of Jerusalem / Dome of the Rock) checked first; corroborated by Britannica 'Old City of Jerusalem', en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dome_of_the_Rock and /Old_City_of_Jerusalem. Verified: four quarters (Armenian SW, Christian NW w/ Holy Sepulchre, Muslim NE largest w/ Temple Mount/Al-Aqsa/Dome, Jewish SE); Dome = oldest surviving Islamic architecture.
framing_note: Place = Jerusalem; the Immovable Ladder is the dinner-test payoff. STANCE (vision-mandated): present each faith's claim RESPECTFULLY on its own terms -- attribute meaning to the tradition ('Jews hold...', 'Muslims hold...'), no smug secular dismissal, no advocacy for any side. The topic is the timeless SACRED GEOGRAPHY (quarters, wall, spring, stone), NOT modern sovereignty/current events -- keep borders out. Distractors live as other Old City sites (Damascus Gate, Al-Aqsa, Mount of Olives, the Cardo) and other walled old cities.
history_overlap: The Second Temple and its Roman destruction (70 AD) may be a history-bank episode -- keep the Western Wall rung anchored to the surviving PLACE; integrator should check.

name: Alexandria
strand: Cities of the Middle East & North Africa
scope: Alexander's Mediterranean city, home to two vanished wonders. T2: founded by Alexander the Great in 331 BC, Alexandria guarded its harbor with a ~110 m tower of fire -- one of the Seven Wonders -- the PHAROS lighthouse. T3: the Pharos toppled in a chain of medieval EARTHQUAKES, and its stones were reused to build a fort still standing on the very spot -- Fort Qaitbay. T3: Alexandria held the ancient world's greatest LIBRARY, which set out to collect every book on Earth. T4 (dinner-test): ships entering the harbor were searched for scrolls, which were COPIED for the Library -- and often the original kept and the copy handed back. T4: under the modern city lie Roman burial halls that blend Egyptian, Greek, and Roman art in one carved tomb -- the CATACOMBS of Kom el Shoqafa. T4: a lone 25 m granite column the crusaders misnamed still stands -- 'POMPEY'S PILLAR,' actually raised for the emperor Diocletian. T5: it was in Alexandria that Eratosthenes measured the whole EARTH'S size from the angle of a shadow, around 240 BC.
source: Grokipedia (Lighthouse of Alexandria) checked first; corroborated by en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighthouse_of_Alexandria, Britannica 'Lighthouse of Alexandria'. Verified: ~100-130 m Pharos, Seven Wonders, damaged by quakes AD 956-1303 (destructive 1303), Fort Qaitbay built ~1477 from its stones; founded 331 BC.
framing_note: Place = Alexandria; the ships-searched-for-scrolls rung is the dinner-test. Accuracy rail: the Library's loss was GRADUAL (fires, funding decline, neglect over centuries) -- do NOT assert one dramatic burning by Caesar destroyed it; the Pharos fell to earthquakes. 'Pompey's Pillar' is a genuine MISNAME -- flag it. Distractors live as the other Seven Wonders and other ancient libraries (Pergamon, Ashurbanipal's at Nineveh, Celsus at Ephesus).
history_overlap: Cleopatra / Caesar episodes belong to history -- keep these rungs anchored to the PLACE and its structures to avoid overlap; integrator should check.

name: Isfahan
strand: Cities of the Middle East & North Africa
scope: A Safavid Persian capital so grand a proverb calls it 'half the world.' T2 (invert): Isfahan is so beautiful a Persian proverb says seeing it is like seeing HALF the world -- 'Isfahan nesf-e jahan.' T2: its heart is one of the largest public squares on Earth, ~89,600 m2, laid out around 1600 by Shah Abbas -- NAQSH-E JAHAN Square. T3: on the square's south side rises a mosque whose great dome is skinned in tens of thousands of blue tiles -- the SHAH (Imam) Mosque. T3 (dinner-test): the square doubled as a royal POLO ground, and stone goalposts from 400 years ago still stand at each end. T4: the jewel-like SHEIKH LOTFOLLAH Mosque has no minaret and no courtyard -- because it was the shah's PRIVATE family mosque. T4: the Zayanderud river is crossed by Safavid bridges that double as dams and gathering places -- the 33-arch SI-O-SE-POL. T5 (craft born here): those glowing domes get their color from lustrous glazed TILEWORK in turquoise and cobalt, a Persian craft perfected here.
source: Grokipedia (Shah Abbas Square) checked first; corroborated by en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naqsh-e_Jahan_Square, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Si-o-se-pol, UNESCO 'Meidan Emam, Esfahan'. Verified: square 160x560 m = 89,600 m2, built 1598-1629 under Shah Abbas I; four monuments (Shah Mosque S, Ali Qapu W, Sheikh Lotfollah E, Qeysarie Gate/Bazaar N); Si-o-se-pol 33 arches, 1599-1602.
framing_note: Place = Isfahan; the square-was-a-polo-field (goalposts still standing) rung is the dinner-test. Accuracy rail: Naqsh-e Jahan ~89,600 m2, Shah Abbas I, ~1600 -- keep exact; invert the 'half the world' proverb rather than asking 'what is Isfahan's nickname?'. Distractors live as other Isfahan monuments (Ali Qapu, Khaju Bridge, Chehel Sotoun) and other great squares (Tiananmen, Red Square) and Persian sites (Persepolis, Shiraz).

name: Marrakech
strand: Cities of the Middle East & North Africa
scope: A Moroccan 'Red City' of ochre walls at the foot of the Atlas. T2 (invert & earth-material): Marrakech is the 'Red City' because its walls and houses are built from local red-OCHRE earth (rammed pise). T2: its great square fills each night with storytellers, snake charmers, musicians, and food stalls -- a living theatre UNESCO named a Masterpiece of Oral Heritage -- JEMAA EL-FNA. T3: above the medina rises the 77 m minaret of the 12th-century KOUTOUBIA Mosque, the model for sister towers in Spain and Morocco. T3: the medina is a walled maze of covered SOUKS organized by craft -- a dyers' alley, a metalworkers' alley, a slipper alley. T4: Marrakech was founded around 1070 by the ALMORAVIDS, desert Berbers, as a caravan capital between the Sahara and the Atlas. T4 (dinner-test, teach the term): the city drinks Atlas snowmelt carried for miles underground through gently sloping tunnels -- a KHETTARA (qanat) water system.
source: Grokipedia (Marrakesh) checked first; corroborated by en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kutubiyya_Mosque, UNESCO 'Medina of Marrakesh', en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marrakesh. Verified: Koutoubia minaret 77 m; Jemaa el-Fna UNESCO Oral & Intangible Heritage (2001); red walls built by Ali ibn Yusuf 1122-23; founded 1070-72 by the Almoravids.
framing_note: Place = Marrakech; Jemaa el-Fna as a living oral-heritage theatre is the memorable payoff (and the khettara is the teach-a-term T4). Accuracy rail: Koutoubia = 77 m; Jemaa el-Fna's UNESCO honor is for its LIVING oral tradition. Lane border: the square's food stalls exist, but a tagine/couscous rung is COOKING -- keep answers on the PLACE (the square, the ochre walls, the underground water). Distractors live as other Moroccan sites (Fes, Chefchaouen, Ait Benhaddou) and other famous squares.

name: Fes
strand: Cities of the Middle East & North Africa
scope: Morocco's medieval spiritual capital and its labyrinth medina. T2 (invert & dinner-test): in Fes stands what Guinness records as the world's OLDEST still-running university -- founded in 859 AD by a WOMAN, Fatima al-Fihri -- AL-QARAWIYYIN. T3: Fes el-Bali is one of the world's largest CAR-FREE urban areas -- a medieval medina of thousands of tangled lanes where deliveries still move by DONKEY. T3: the city's leather is still cured in medieval stone vats of colored dye you smell before you see -- the CHOUARA TANNERY, worked by hand for a thousand years. T4: al-Qarawiyyin's LIBRARY holds manuscripts over a thousand years old -- one of the oldest working libraries on Earth. T4: Fes was founded around 789 by the IDRISID dynasty and became Morocco's scholarly and spiritual heart. T5 (engineering): the medina's fountains, mills, and tanneries all run on the Oued Fes river, deliberately SPLIT into channels threaded through the old city.
source: Grokipedia (University of al-Qarawiyyin) checked first; corroborated by en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_al-Qarawiyyin, World History Encyclopedia 'Fatima Al-Fihri and Al-Qarawiyyin University', en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chouara_Tannery. Verified: founded 859 by Fatima al-Fihri, Guinness 'oldest continually operating higher-learning institution'; Chouara Tannery in Fes el-Bali, hand methods unchanged since medieval times.
framing_note: Place = Fes; the oldest-university-founded-by-a-woman-in-859 rung is the dinner-test. Accuracy rail: al-Qarawiyyin founded 859 by Fatima al-Fihri, Guinness-recognized oldest continually operating -- keep exact. Lane: leatherwork is a craft BORN here (place-anchored, fine), but keep it about the tannery/place, not a how-to-tan product ladder. Distractors live as other ancient universities (Bologna, Oxford, Al-Azhar, Nalanda) and other Moroccan medinas.

name: Damascus
strand: Cities of the Middle East & North Africa
scope: A leading claimant for the oldest continuously inhabited city on Earth. T2 (invert): people have lived in Damascus without a break for thousands of years -- habitation reaches back before 2000 BC -- making it a top claimant for the world's OLDEST continuously inhabited city. T3: at its heart stands one of the oldest and grandest mosques on Earth, built 705-715 AD on an old temple-then-church site -- the UMAYYAD (Great) MOSQUE. T3 (dinner-test): inside that mosque is a shrine that Christians AND Muslims alike hold to contain the head of JOHN THE BAPTIST. T4: a Roman-era avenue still crosses the old city -- the 'STREET CALLED STRAIGHT' (Via Recta), named in the Bible's story of Paul. T4 (earth-process): Damascus is a desert OASIS fed by the Barada river spilling from the Anti-Lebanon mountains -- the green Ghouta that let a city survive on the desert's edge. T5 (craft/trade born here): patterned 'DAMASCUS STEEL' blades, prized for watery ripples in the metal, were forged and traded through the city -- and the original recipe is now LOST.
source: Grokipedia (Damascus / Umayyad Mosque) checked first; corroborated by UNESCO 'Ancient City of Damascus', en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umayyad_Mosque, Britannica 'Great Mosque of Damascus'. Verified: origins 3rd millennium BC (Tell Ramad far older); Umayyad Mosque 705-715 AD by al-Walid I, earliest surviving stone mosque, John-the-Baptist head shrine; Via Recta the Roman decumanus, ~1,500 m.
framing_note: Place = Damascus; the John-the-Baptist-head shrine is the dinner-test. Accuracy rail: attribute the relic AS tradition ('Christians and Muslims believe...'); Damascus-steel's exact crucible technique is genuinely LOST/debated -- say so, don't assert a method. Keep it TIMELESS place geography -- no rung touching the modern war. Distractors live as other 'oldest city' claimants (Jericho, Aleppo, Byblos, Uruk) and other great early mosques.
history_overlap: Paul's conversion on the Straight Street may be a history/theology episode -- one rung; keep it anchored to the PLACE (the surviving Roman avenue); integrator should check.

name: Baghdad
strand: Cities of the Middle East & North Africa
scope: The Abbasid capital where a golden age of learning was born on the Tigris. T2 (named shape): Caliph al-Mansur built Baghdad in 762 as a perfectly ROUND city -- circular walls with the palace at the exact center. T3: Baghdad's HOUSE OF WISDOM gathered scholars who translated Greek, Persian, and Indian books into Arabic and pushed math and astronomy forward. T3 (dinner-test, born here): a Baghdad scholar, al-Khwarizmi, wrote the book that gave us the word 'ALGEBRA' -- and his own name became the word 'algorithm.' T4 (vivid): in 1258 the Mongols sacked Baghdad and hurled so many books into the Tigris that the river was said to run BLACK WITH INK. T4 (earth/place): Baghdad sits between the Tigris and Euphrates in MESOPOTAMIA -- 'the land between the rivers,' the ancient cradle of cities. T5 (surviving place): one Abbasid college still stands -- the 13th-century MUSTANSIRIYA MADRASA on the Tigris, among the oldest universities on Earth still in use.
source: Grokipedia (House of Wisdom / Baghdad) checked first; corroborated by Britannica 'Bayt al-Hikmah', en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Wisdom. Verified: al-Mansur's Round City founded 762; House of Wisdom flourished under Harun al-Rashid & al-Ma'mun, largest book repository by mid-9th c, al-Khwarizmi a patron; Mongol sack 1258, Tigris 'ran black with ink.'
framing_note: Place = Baghdad; the Tigris-ran-black-with-ink rung is the dinner-test. Accuracy rail: the House of Wisdom and Round City are GONE -- anchor rungs to the enduring Tigris/Mesopotamia setting, to the surviving Mustansiriya, and to creations genuinely BORN here (algebra), and label vanished wonders AS vanished so no rung implies you can visit them. Distractors live as other centers of learning (Cordoba, Al-Azhar, Timbuktu) and other Mesopotamian cities (Babylon, Ur, Nineveh).
history_overlap: The Abbasid golden age and the 1258 Mongol sack may be history-bank episodes -- keep the PLACE (round city, river, madrasa) the anchor; integrator should check.

name: Mecca -- the Kaaba & qibla
strand: Cities of the Middle East & North Africa
scope: A single point in Arabia toward which roughly a quarter of humanity turns to pray. T2 (invert): every mosque on Earth is built so worshippers face ONE point -- a cube-shaped building in Mecca called the KAABA. T3 (teach the term): the direction Muslims face in prayer, toward the Kaaba, has its own name, and each mosque marks it with a wall niche called a mihrab -- the QIBLA. T3: once a year millions of pilgrims converge on Mecca in one of the largest human gatherings on the planet -- the HAJJ. T4 (dinner-test): pilgrims circle the Kaaba SEVEN times counter-clockwise -- a rite called TAWAF. T4: set into the Kaaba's eastern corner is a dark stone pilgrims try to touch or point to -- the BLACK STONE (al-Hajar al-Aswad). T4 (earth/place + tradition): beside the Kaaba is a spring held to have flowed for thousands of years in the desert valley -- the WELL OF ZAMZAM.
source: Grokipedia (Kaaba / Qibla) checked first; corroborated by en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qibla, /Kaaba, /Black_Stone, /Zamzam_Well, Britannica 'Qiblah'. Verified: Kaaba at center of Masjid al-Haram = qibla for all mosques (marked by the mihrab); Hajj >2 M/yr, one of the largest gatherings; tawaf = 7 counter-clockwise circuits; Black Stone in the eastern corner; Zamzam ~21 m east of the Kaaba.
framing_note: Place = Mecca/Kaaba; the tawaf (seven circuits) -- or the fact that ONE point orients every mosque on Earth -- is the dinner-test. STANCE (vision-mandated): describe the Kaaba, Hajj, and Zamzam RESPECTFULLY on Islam's own terms -- attribute belief to the tradition ('Muslims face...', 'pilgrims believe...'), no smug secular dismissal AND no devotional advertising. The geography hook is real and neutral: a single coordinate organizes sacred orientation worldwide. Non-Muslims may not enter Mecca -- state that plainly as a true place-fact. Distractors live as other holy sites (Medina, Jerusalem, Karbala, Najaf) and other pilgrimage terms.

name: Cappadocia & Derinkuyu
strand: Cities of the Middle East & North Africa
scope: A Turkish moonscape of volcanic rock hiding whole cities underground. T2 (named landform, invert): central Turkey's Cappadocia bristles with tall stone spires shaped like mushrooms and chimneys, sculpted by erosion -- FAIRY CHIMNEYS. T3 (teach the term, earth-process): the spires exist because the ground is soft volcanic-ash rock -- TUFF -- easy for wind, water, and human hands to carve. T3: people hollowed the soft rock into homes and churches -- the Goreme valley holds cave CHURCHES painted with 1,000-year-old frescoes. T4 (dinner-test): whole CITIES were carved straight DOWN -- DERINKUYU descends about 85 m through 8+ levels and could shelter ~20,000 people with their livestock. T4: great round STONE DOORS could be rolled across the tunnels from the inside to seal the underground city against invaders. T4: 52 vertical SHAFTS carried fresh air and water to the deepest levels, so families could live below ground for months. T5 (earth-process): the soft rock came from ancient eruptions of nearby volcanoes like Mount Erciyes, which buried the region in ash that hardened into tuff.
source: Grokipedia (Derinkuyu) surfaced and checked; corroborated by en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derinkuyu_underground_city, Atlas Obscura, UNESCO 'Goreme National Park and the Rock Sites of Cappadocia'. Verified: Derinkuyu ~85 m deep, 8 visitable levels (18+ suspected), ~20,000 capacity, 52 ventilation shafts, carved into volcanic tuff; fairy chimneys = tuff eroded from ash of Erciyes/Hasan volcanoes.
framing_note: Place = Cappadocia; the 20,000-person underground city (Derinkuyu) with rolling stone doors is the dinner-test. This is the sub-strand's EARTH-SCIENCE keystone -- teach 'tuff' before testing it. Accuracy rail: Derinkuyu ~85 m / 8 open levels (more suspected), 52 shafts -- keep those and don't inflate. Distractors live as other carved-rock landscapes (Meteora, Petra, Bandiagara cliffs) and other underground places (Paris Catacombs, Coober Pedy, Naours).

name: Old Sanaa
strand: Cities of the Middle East & North Africa
scope: A Yemeni highland capital of decorated mud-brick towers, lived in for 2,500 years. T2 (named place-form): Old Sanaa is packed with thousands of TOWER HOUSES five to nine stories tall, built of earth and brick and iced with white gypsum patterns like gingerbread. T3 (teach the term): their upper rooms glow through fan-shaped stained-glass windows set in gypsum -- QAMARIYA windows. T3 (label legend): people have lived in Sanaa without a break for more than 2,500 years -- legend even credits its founding to Shem, a son of Noah. T4: you enter the walled old city through a great fortified gate -- BAB AL-YEMEN. T4 (engineering): the lower floors are heavy STONE and the upper floors lighter rammed earth and fired brick -- a design that let mud towers rise nine stories and stand for centuries. T5 (dinner-test): the Great Mosque of Sanaa, one of Islam's oldest, hid in its roof a PALIMPSEST -- an early Quran written over an even older erased text (the 'Sanaa manuscript').
source: Grokipedia (Old City of Sana'a) checked first; corroborated by UNESCO WHS 'Old City of Sana'a', en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sana'a, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sana'a_manuscript. Verified: 6,000+ multi-story tower houses (stone base, rammed-earth/fired-brick upper), white gypsum decoration, qamariya windows, inhabited 2,500+ yrs, UNESCO 1986 (in danger); Sanaa palimpsest = early Quranic manuscript.
framing_note: Place = Sanaa; the qamariya windows and the roof-hidden Sanaa palimpsest are the memorable payoffs. Accuracy rail: 2,500+ yrs inhabited is solid; the Shem/son-of-Noah founding is LEGEND -- label it. Keep it timeless place geography -- no rung touching the current war. Distractors live as other mud/earth-brick cities (Shibam, Djenne, Timbuktu, Bam).

name: Persepolis
strand: Cities of the Middle East & North Africa
scope: The ceremonial capital of the Persian Empire, burned at the height of its glory. T2: in the Iranian highlands stand the ruins of the Persian Empire's grand ceremonial capital, begun by Darius I around 518 BC -- PERSEPOLIS. T3: you reach it on a monumental double STAIRCASE cut so gently that horses could ride up, its walls lined with carved reliefs. T3 (dinner-test): the Apadana stairway shows a parade of 23 SUBJECT NATIONS bringing gifts -- rows of Medes, Nubians, and Indians, each carved in their own dress. T4 (named guardians): visitors passed through a portal guarded by giant winged, human-headed BULLS -- the GATE OF ALL NATIONS, raised by Xerxes. T4 (label disputed): Persepolis burned in 330 BC when Alexander the Great took it -- whether by a drunken accident or as deliberate revenge for Persia's burning of Athens is still DEBATED.
source: Grokipedia (Persepolis) checked; corroborated by en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persepolis, UNESCO WHS 'Persepolis', World History Encyclopedia 'Persepolis'. Verified: Achaemenid ceremonial capital, begun by Darius I ~518 BC; Apadana tribute-bearer reliefs (23 delegations); Gate of All Nations (Xerxes) with lamassu; destroyed by fire in 330 BC under Alexander (cause disputed).
framing_note: Place = Persepolis; the carved parade of 23 tribute nations is the dinner-test. Accuracy rail: Darius I ~518 BC; the CAUSE of the 330 BC fire (accident vs. revenge for Athens) is genuinely disputed -- present it as debated, don't pick a side. Distractors live as other ancient Persian/Near-East capitals and ruins (Pasargadae, Susa, Babylon, Palmyra).
history_overlap: Alexander's conquest of the Persian Empire may be a history-bank episode -- keep the PLACE (the palace, staircase, gate) the anchor; integrator should check.

name: Shibam
strand: Cities of the Middle East & North Africa
scope: A 16th-century walled town of mud-brick high-rises, the 'Manhattan of the Desert.' T3 (dinner-test, named place): in a Yemeni desert valley stands a cluster of ~500 mud-brick TOWER BLOCKS five to eleven stories high, packed tight inside a wall -- explorer Freya Stark called it the 'MANHATTAN OF THE DESERT' (Shibam). T4 (invert): Shibam is the OLDEST city on Earth built vertically -- the first true skyscraper city, raised entirely from sun-dried MUD BRICK about 500 years ago. T5 (engineering): the towers are wider at the base and thinner as they climb -- the walls TAPER because the upper bricks are made smaller, spreading the weight so mud can stand ~30 m tall.
source: Grokipedia (Shibam) checked; corroborated by National Geographic 'This Ancient Mud Skyscraper City is the Manhattan of the Desert', en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shibam, ArchDaily. Verified: ~500 mud-brick tower houses 5-11 stories, 16th c, oldest metropolis built vertically, walls taper upward, Freya Stark coined 'Manhattan of the desert' in the 1930s.
framing_note: Place = Shibam; the 'Manhattan of the Desert' mud-brick skyscrapers ARE the dinner-test. Accuracy rail: ~500 towers, 5-11 stories, sun-dried mud brick, 16th c, tapering walls; attribute the nickname to Freya Stark. Distinct from Sanaa (decorated tower-house capital) -- this ladder is the SKYSCRAPER-cluster gem. Distractors live as other earthen architecture (Sanaa, Djenne's Great Mosque, Taos Pueblo, Bam citadel).

name: Dubai
strand: Cities of the Middle East & North Africa
scope: A former pearl-diving port turned instant desert megacity of record-breaking engineering. T2 (invert): rising straight from the desert coast of the UAE is the TALLEST building in the world, 828 m of steel and glass -- the BURJ KHALIFA. T3 (dinner-test): off Dubai's shore engineers built a human-made island shaped like a PALM TREE, so large you can pick it out from space -- Palm Jumeirah. T3 (place-history): within living memory Dubai was a small port whose divers made their living hunting the Gulf's oyster beds -- PEARL DIVING -- until oil and then trade transformed it. T4 (earth/place): Dubai sits on the hot, shallow PERSIAN GULF, whose warm salty water and pearl-oyster beds made the coast rich long before any skyscraper.
source: Grokipedia (Burj Khalifa / Dubai) checked; standing knowledge corroborated by en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burj_Khalifa and /Palm_Jumeirah (web-search budget exhausted before a live re-verify). Facts used: Burj Khalifa 828 m, world's tallest since 2010; Palm Jumeirah artificial archipelago; Dubai a pre-oil pearling/trading port on the Persian Gulf.
framing_note: Place = Dubai; the palm-shaped human-made island you can see from space is the dinner-test. This is the strand's deliberate MODERN contrast (engineering marvel vs. ancient marvels). Accuracy rail: Burj Khalifa 828 m, tallest since 2010 -- keep exact. Lane/tone: keep answers to concrete place/engineering and the pearling past, NOT luxury-brand or mall advertising. Distractors live as other tall towers (Shanghai Tower, Petronas, Empire State) and other Gulf cities / artificial islands (Abu Dhabi, Doha, The World islands).
